findings.text: follow-on: the reviewed run's manifest `artifacts:` line names the figure at docs/figures/lane-and-model-routing/catalogue-declares-lanes.svg, but the delivered file is docs/figures/lane-and-model-routing/catalogue-declares-lanes/lanes-and-aliases.svg — the second evidence commit moved it inside the node directory and the artifacts line was not updated. `changed_paths` names the directory correctly and the fragment references the file at its real project-absolute src, so this is a record-accuracy drift only, not a missing deliverable.
follow-on: the fragment reads "hand-clear-copied LaneModelConfig's field list", a typo for "hand-copied"; harmless, but the landed record is the artifact a later reader opens.

item_verdicts.call_sites: verified 3 production references: `aliases` joins `_KEYED_MAPS` at reckon/flight.py:60 so the map key is injected as `name` before pydantic validation; `_lane_model_keys()` at reckon/flight.py:1304 derives LANE_MODEL_KEYS from the generated LaneModelConfig; the catalogue declares `lanes:` at docs/state/reckon/model-catalogue.yaml:93.
item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base 8a4140a93; the reviewed run gained three commits. 57c0b36b9 (code) regroups the catalogue under lanes with a default model each and adds a top-level aliases table mapping each legacy name to (lane, model_key); the catalogue schema gains an aliases slot and a ModelAlias class, and reckon/_flight_schema.py + docs/_shared/flight.schema.json are regenerated from it; reckon/flight.py replaces the hand-copied LANE_MODEL_KEYS tuple with a derivation from the generated LaneModelConfig.model_fields and lists aliases in _KEYED_MAPS; tests/test_catalogue_declares_lanes.py is new and tests/test_flight_lanes.py gains the derivation-pinning case. 2a2a39c88 and f94c0926c are docs-only (the evidence fragment and its figure, the latter moving the figure into the node directory).
item_verdicts.done_when: the plan section 2 done-when names three checks. (1) `reckon flight --project reckon` identical to base: reproduced independently — the backends: block is byte-identical base vs head (8 entries, sorted-dump diff empty), and resolving the head catalogue with `lanes:`/`aliases:` stripped yields config and provenance equal to the full head catalogue (positive control: the two catalogue dicts differ). The run's own flight-compare.txt shows config/layers/project/provenance/undeclared_meteredness/warnings all SAME, with the only difference being availability.clive.lane_headroom (7->3), a live serving-lane probe, not a resolved value. (2) catalogue provenance shows the same leaves: SAME provenance in flight-compare.txt, consistent with the backends block being unchanged. (3) a test asserts every alias resolves to a declared lane and model: tests/test_catalogue_declares_lanes.py::test_every_alias_resolves_to_a_declared_lane_and_model asserts the table is exactly the seven names, each lane is declared, each name equals `<lane>-<key>`, and each live alias names a key the lane declares, with the three retired names (terra, spark, glm) asserted to be exactly the names with no declared model behind them. Negative control reproduced here: deleting lanes.claude.models.opus in a copy and running via RECKON_CATALOGUE_FIXTURE reddens three cases including the alias test (3 failed, 1 passed, EXIT=1).
item_verdicts.goal: the section's goal is that the model catalogue declare lanes with a default model each and add the alias table section 7 reads, keeping the backends: blocks so the two groupings compare. The delta completes it: lanes.claude (default sonnet; sonnet/opus/haiku), lanes.codex (default sol; sol/astra/luna) and lanes.clive (default flash; flash) are declared at docs/state/reckon/model-catalogue.yaml:93, each model carrying the same model/effort/alias/budget_group its backends: entry already had, and the eight backends: blocks are unchanged. The aliases: table maps claude-opus, claude-haiku, codex-astra, codex-luna (live) and codex-terra, codex-spark, clive-glm (retired) each to a (lane, model_key) pair. The catalogue schema had no slot, so reckon/schema/flight.yaml gained a top-level aliases slot (range ModelAlias, inlined) and a ModelAlias class with lane/model_key, and the two generated artifacts were regenerated rather than hand-edited.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the three commits (57c0b36b9, 2a2a39c88, f94c0926c), the nine changed paths, the 15-file gate command with head 407 passed 0 skipped EXIT=0 against base 402 passed 0 skipped EXIT=0, names gate-head.log/gate-base.log/negative-control.log, and declares baseline_suite and after_suite arms each completed with failure_count 0 and empty failure_ids. One drift: the artifacts: line names the figure at its pre-move path (see findings).
item_verdicts.write_paths: the nine changed paths match the run's granted orientation_write_paths exactly. The plan section 2 names only docs/state/reckon/model-catalogue.yaml and tests/test_catalogue_declares_lanes.py, so seven touched paths (reckon/schema/flight.yaml, reckon/_flight_schema.py, docs/_shared/flight.schema.json, reckon/flight.py, tests/test_flight_lanes.py, the evidence fragment, the figure) lie outside the plan's stated write paths; the dispatch granted them, and the schema and generated artifacts were necessary — the catalogue could not carry the new slots otherwise.

justifications.durability: the change is guarded where it could rot. The two LinkML round-trip tests compare the committed pydantic module and JSON Schema byte-for-byte against regeneration from reckon/schema/flight.yaml, and executed rather than skipped here (gen-pydantic and gen-json-schema resolve on the main checkout's .venv/bin); the derived-keys test pins LANE_MODEL_KEYS to LaneModelConfig.model_fields, closing the section 1 review's hand-mirror finding; the inertness of the new blocks is pinned by a test that strips them and demands an equal resolution. Residual: the test's `_backend_lane_model` helper infers a backend's lane by name prefix, which holds only while lanes are named by dialect — a deliberate plan decision, not a defect.
justifications.evidence: evidence is complete and the load-bearing parts were reproduced here rather than read. The head gate re-ran at HEAD f94c0926 (which carries the two docs commits beyond the run's measured 57c0b36b93): 407 passed, 0 skipped, EXIT=0. The no-value-moves proof was re-derived independently — backends block byte-identical base vs head, and stripping lanes:/aliases: from the head catalogue leaves config and provenance equal, with a positive control that the two catalogues differ. The negative control was re-run: deleting lanes.claude.models.opus reddens three catalogue cases (EXIT=1), which the head arm passes. The two round-trip tests were run explicitly and pass. The run's own flight-compare.txt attributes the one differing key (availability.clive.lane_headroom 7->3) to a live probe, which is consistent with the saved artifacts.
justifications.fit: the added names describe mechanism — lanes, aliases, ModelAlias, model_key, _lane_model_keys — with no version, plan, sprint or ticket identifier; the new schema slots and class match the file's existing noun idiom, and the generated artifacts stay generated. The lazy import of LaneModelConfig inside _lane_model_keys mirrors the module's existing local-import pattern and avoids a cycle. Minor: a typo ("hand-clear-copied") survives in the evidence fragment (see findings).
justifications.goal_fidelity: the delta completes section 2 without adding a routing axis: the catalogue now declares three lanes each with a default model and its models keyed (docs/state/reckon/model-catalogue.yaml:93), keeps the eight backends: blocks unchanged, and adds the seven-name alias table section 7 resolves stored rows through. The schema change is the minimum the declaration needs (one slot, one class, regenerated outputs), and the section 1 hand-mirror finding is closed by deriving LANE_MODEL_KEYS from the generated model.
justifications.reuse: the change extends existing machinery rather than adding a parallel path: aliases joins the existing _KEYED_MAPS mechanism, the artifacts are produced by the existing scripts/regen_flight_schema.py, LANE_MODEL_KEYS now reads the generated model instead of restating it, and the new test reuses the flight.resolve entry point. No duplicated capability.
justifications.scope_discipline: all nine changed paths fall inside the run's granted write scope, and none outside it, but seven of the nine lie outside the plan section 2's own stated write paths (model-catalogue.yaml, tests/test_catalogue_declares_lanes.py). The expansion was authorised by the dispatch and was necessary — the catalogue schema had no slot for the new blocks, so the schema source and its two generated artifacts had to move with it — but it remains a real deviation from the plan's stated scope and is recorded as such.
